title: TaskCraft: Automated Generation of Agentic Tasks
claim: A task is solved by parsing it into a tool input, executing a tool for context, then reasoning over that context to an answer.
layout: Single flow looping down-left then up-right; robot icons mark each LLM step
description: A single tool invocation drawn as a looping flow, with a worked stock-price example. The Task q box (stacked card, question-mark icon, green quoted text 'Stock with highest price increase today?') is at top left. An arrow runs down through an LLM Parsing robot to the Input Index i_T box ('Nasdaq Stock Market Data'). From there, a Tool Execution gear icon leads to the Tool Context C box (INTC, NVDA, TSLA percentages). A Tool List panel (PDF, Image, Web tools in orange, blue and green) sits in the middle. A bottom LLM Reasoning robot receives the task and the context, and a dashed arrow leads to the Implicit Relation R box. A second LLM Reasoning robot at right produces the Answer a box at top right (lightbulb icon, 'INTC (+10.44%)'). Blue handwritten-style labels name the steps, and gray arrows with dashed ones for the relation.
caption: Execution flow of a single tool invocation. The agent extracts the input index iT (e.g., document name, webpage title) for invoking tool T, focusing solely on steps that yield valid tool context. Executing T with iT retrieves context C, enabling the LLM to infer the relationship R and produce the final result a.
abstract: Agentic tasks, which require multi-step problem solving with autonomy, tool use, and adaptive reasoning, are becoming increasingly central to the advancement of NLP and AI. However, existing instruction data lacks tool interaction, and current agentic benchmarks rely on costly human annotation, limiting their scalability. We introduce \textsc{TaskCraft}, an automated workflow for generating difficulty-scalable, multi-tool, and verifiable agentic tasks with execution trajectories. TaskCraft expands atomic tasks using depth-based and width-based extensions to create structurally and hierarchically complex challenges. Empirical results show that these tasks improve prompt optimization in the generation workflow and enhance supervised fine-tuning of agentic foundation models. We present a large-scale synthetic dataset of approximately 36,000 tasks with varying difficulty to support future research on agent tuning and evaluation.
